# Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK — facts

> Source-anchored units about Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK: 22 across 4 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-06 · 22 units · 4 sources · rights: quote -->

## Definitions

- [statement] Memory visibility is project-bounded: `org` means readable within the project, not across projects. Semantic, episodic, and procedural writes default to `private`, while taxonomic writes default to `org`. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/add-features/memory-types.md · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK · also: https://pypi.org/project/agent-engine-sdk-memory/

## How it works

- [statement] The SDK documentation says bound `session_id` is inherited for conversation I/O but not for episodic or semantic search. Episodic search requires an explicit call argument for session filtering because consolidated episodes are session-unscoped. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://pypi.org/project/agent-engine-sdk-memory/ · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Install with `pip install agent-engine-sdk-memory` and import `Memory` and `MemoryRequestContext` from `agent_engine_sdk_memory`. The SDK documentation describes runtime dependencies limited to `pydantic` and `httpx`. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-sdk-memory.md · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK · also: https://pypi.org/project/agent-engine-sdk-memory/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] SDK documentation says failed background extraction does not undo a successful turn write. Environmental failures get bounded retries; content-determined failures are recorded without retry. A stored memory that lacks an embedding can appear through text or hybrid retrieval but cannot appear through semantic-only retrieval. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-sdk-memory.md · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK · also: https://pypi.org/project/agent-engine-sdk-memory/
- [statement] HyperFRAME Research cautions that persistent agent memory can retain mistaken conclusions, outdated preferences or sensitive information; this is an analyst risk assessment, not an observed incident in this service. (low confidence) — https://hyperframeresearch.com/2026/10/01/mongodb-brings-agent-memory-and-governance-into-atlas/ · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Binding a request context creates a new scoped handle without changing the original. Identity resolves from call arguments, then bound context, then runtime context; blank values fall through rather than clearing a bound identity. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-sdk-memory.md · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MongoDB documents a persistent memory service that can run independently of an agent deployment; the standalone `agent-engine-sdk-memory` Python package records conversation turns and retrieves context for external applications. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/add-features/memory-only.md · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-sdk-memory.md
- [statement] The SDK exposes a Memory facade and depends only on pydantic and httpx, avoiding a dependency on the full platform stack. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-sdk-memory.md · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK
- [statement] Memory has raw, chronological short-term conversation history and durable long-term knowledge. Background processing summarizes conversation snapshots and uses an LLM to extract semantic facts, episodic histories, procedural workflows, and taxonomic terms; applications can also write long-term memories directly. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/add-features/memory-types.md · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-sdk-memory.md
- [statement] Background extraction processes conversation snapshots asynchronously. A successful turn write does not mean its extracted long-term knowledge is ready for the next turn; use short-term memory for recent conversational context. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-sdk-memory.md · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/add-features/memory-types.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/add-features/memory-only.md
- [statement] `build_context` and `build_context_from_sources` assemble prompt-ready context by ranking, de-duplicating, and budgeting matches; `search` and per-type searches return records. The default context sources are semantic and episodic; STM, procedural, and taxonomic sources require explicit inclusion. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/add-features/memory-types.md · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK · also: https://pypi.org/project/agent-engine-sdk-memory/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-sdk-memory.md
- [statement] The per-source context builder accepts separate retrieval modes, filters and candidate counts. Semantic retrieval matches embeddings, text retrieval matches words, and hybrid retrieval combines their rankings. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-sdk-memory.md · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK
- [statement] Hosted standalone connections use a service-account access token and project identifier. Local development connects to the CLI-managed proxy using a base URL with no project identifier; platform-deployed agents instead receive a prewired Memory instance. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/add-features/memory-only.md · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-sdk-memory.md
- [statement] The standalone guide supports custom memory types in hosted mode but excludes them locally. The SDK capability table likewise marks hosted custom-type `save` / `retrieve` as flag-gated, direct mode as unavailable without execution context, and app-bound mode as supported; unsupported operations raise `MemoryNotSupportedError`. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/add-features/memory-only.md · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-sdk-memory.md
- [statement] The SDK reads and writes data but does not configure the memory server. Server settings live in the `memory:` block of `project-config.yaml`; `agentengine memory configure` stores them and `agentengine memory apply` restarts or provisions the runtime to read them. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-sdk-memory.md · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK · also: https://pypi.org/project/agent-engine-sdk-memory/
- [statement] A MongoDB partner example documents using the SDK to connect externally hosted agents to the memory service, with extraction and storage performed server-side. This demonstrates an integration pattern, not independent production-performance validation. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb-partners/config-driven-agents-agentcore-atlas/blob/main/README.md · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK
- [statement] The SDK exposes one `Memory` facade for both external and platform-hosted agents. An external application constructs it and binds conversation identity; a platform agent receives an instance whose invocation identity and transport are supplied by the runtime. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-sdk-memory.md · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/add-features/memory-types.md
- [statement] `bind(ctx)` creates a new scoped handle without changing the original. `record_turn` uses the bound user and session and offers no per-call `user_id` or `visibility` override, so external applications should bind each conversation explicitly. (medium confidence) — https://pypi.org/project/agent-engine-sdk-memory/ · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-sdk-memory.md
- [statement] `build_context_from_sources` accepts a `SourceSpec` per source with its own retrieval `mode`, `metadata_filter`, and `top_k`; modes are `text`, `semantic`, or `hybrid`. Its default mode is semantic, while the SDK recommends hybrid for text-bearing sources to combine paraphrase retrieval with exact-term matching. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://pypi.org/project/agent-engine-sdk-memory/ · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK
- [statement] The SDK documents `max_tokens` as a gross context-construction budget: it subtracts a 500-token formatting reserve and selects whole chunks from what remains. Positive budgets at or below 500 leave no room for memory chunks; larger budgets can still return empty context if no chunk fits. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://pypi.org/project/agent-engine-sdk-memory/ · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK
- [statement] For SDK reads, `user_id` and `visibility` combine as an intersection. Passing `visibility="org"` on a user-bound handle does not union project knowledge with personal memory; the SDK recommends separate reads and merging for that use case. (medium confidence) — https://pypi.org/project/agent-engine-sdk-memory/ · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-sdk-memory.md
- [statement] The memory guide says a deployed agent invoked using a service account uses that service account as its memory user identity and ignores invoke-supplied end-user IDs. It distinguishes the standalone memory service, which accepts explicit end-user and session IDs, and recommends that path for end-user isolation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/add-features/memory-types.md · keywords: Agent Engine memory service and the agent-engine-sdk-memory Python SDK
